title: The question means last proximate disposition — not Rivetus’s present-remission fiducia
source_text: CIX. Sed inter actus fidei quidam sunt qui propius, alii qui remotius ad justificationem disponunt & praeparant. Quum vero apud Reformatos quaeritur, quis sit actus ille, per quem justificamur, sensus quaestionis est, ratione cujus actus, fides sit ultima illa & proxima dispositio, ad quam immediate & infallibiliter sequitur justificatio? Hunc autem actum Theologi jam dicti, Rivetus, Wendelinus, Paraeus, Maresius, volunt esse fiduciam, qua nobis persuademus peccata in praesenti speciatim nobis remitti; cui sententiae propter rationes jam dictas, assentiri non possumus.
pass_a_gloss: But among the acts of faith some dispose and prepare to justification more nearly, others more remotely. When among the Reformed it is asked what that act is by which we are justified, the sense of the question is: by reason of which act is faith that last and nearest disposition upon which justification immediately and infallibly follows? But this act the theologians already named — Rivetus, Wendelinus, Paraeus, Maresius — want to be the trust by which we persuade ourselves that sins are being remitted to us specially in the present; to which opinion, for the reasons already stated, we cannot assent.
pass_b_english: Some faith-acts dispose nearer, some remoter, to justification.
Among the Reformed the real question is: which act makes faith the last proximate disposition on which justification follows immediately and infallibly?
Rivet, Wendelin, Pareus, and Maresius answer: present-tense fiducia that my sins are specially being remitted now.
Le Blanc cannot assent, for the reasons already given.
